transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-01 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Miguel Alvarez (Redwood SE), Alyssa Chen (Cascade Head of Platform), Trevor Miles (Cascade Lead DevOps), Nina Park (Cascade Security)

[00:00:05] Sofia Patel: hi everyone thanks for joining, uh we're excited to talk through the private deployment options for Cascade. i think we have 45-ish minutes, so we'll do a quick intro then jump into networking and security.

[00:00:20] Alyssa Chen: yep thanks, appreciate you fitting us in. quick context, we're a mid-size fintech, most infra in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. sensitive data, data residency for eu customers is a must, and security team is picky on egress.

[00:00:45] Miguel Alvarez: awesome. quick intro from my side, i'm miguel, i'm the SE focused on private and dedicated deployments. i work with the infra teams to map networking, peering, private endpoints, that sort of thing.

[00:01:05] Trevor Miles: quick note on our stack — we run prod in a mix of AWS accounts, VPC per team, and we have transit gateway + some direct connect circuits. would prefer not to open public endpoints.

[00:01:30] Nina Park: from security, the main asks: SSO/SAML for console, audit logs retention 1 year, KMS integration for encryption, and HSM usage if we can. also SOC 2 cert is expected.

[00:02:00] Sofia Patel: great — that's inline with what we see. Redwood Private supports a couple patterns: VPC peering between customer VPC and our managed VPC, AWS PrivateLink / interface endpoints for private connectivity, or a deploy-in-customer-account model if you need full control.

[00:02:22] Alyssa Chen: ok can you expand on peering vs PrivateLink — which do customers typically pick?

[00:02:30] Miguel Alvarez: sure — peering is simple if you only need L3 connectivity and CIDR ranges don't overlap; it's direct VPC-to-VPC. PrivateLink uses AWS interface endpoints, it's more controlled and doesn't require route table changes, and it's cross-account friendly. For transit gateway setups we can also support peering via TGW attachments.

[00:03:05] Trevor Miles: our CIDRs overlap across some teams, so peering might be messy. PrivateLink sounds safer. any limits on endpoints?

[00:03:15] Miguel Alvarez: there are practical limits on number of interfaces and ENIs per AZ; we typically recommend a small fleet of interface endpoints per region behind an NLB on our side. performance is fine for API throughput; if you need high qps you can use dedicated capacity which gives pinned GPUs and more predictable egress throughput.

[00:03:45] Alyssa Chen: region question — our EU data should stay in eu-west-1. can Redwood host regional-only deployments?

[00:03:55] Sofia Patel: yes — with Redwood Private we can pin control-plane and inference nodes to a specific region. for hosted customers we have multi-region, but Private lets you restrict everything to customer's chosen region. note that some open models might have optimized kernels only on certain instance types, so we may recommend instance family in the target region.

[00:04:25] Nina Park: okay, and what about egress logging and firewall rules? we need to limit outbound connections from the inference cluster.

[00:04:35] Miguel Alvarez: we support egress via NAT or via explicit firewall/NACL rules. you can route egress through your own NAT/Proxy so you can intercept traffic. we also provide VPC flow logs and application-level auditing in Redwood Console — although the console metadata crosses the control plane; with private deployment that control plane can be isolated or customer-managed depending on SLA.

[00:05:10] Trevor Miles: so we'd want to funnel outbound through our proxy for extra inspection. any need for internet access from model hosts for updates or container pulls?

[00:05:20] Miguel Alvarez: good question. image pulls can be done from private registries — we support ECR in customer account or pre-pulled AMIs. kernel and runtime updates can be scheduled, but we can also offer air-gap patching if you require no public egress.

[00:05:45] Alyssa Chen: KMS integration — we use AWS KMS with strict key policies; do you allow customer-managed keys?

[00:05:55] Sofia Patel: yes, you can use customer-managed KMS keys. for dedicated we integrate with your KMS over the AWS API; for on-prem or air-gapped we have HSM options or an on-prem KMS proxy. we'll document the exact IAM roles needed.

[00:06:20] Nina Park: will Redwood store any plaintext customer data on its control plane? we need to avoid that where possible.

[00:06:28] Miguel Alvarez: typically inference requests are ephemeral; KV cache and logs can be configured to not persist. with Private deployment the control plane metadata can be routed to your logging infrastructure, and logs can be forwarded to your S3 or SIEM. we'll provide config flags to disable retention.

[00:06:55] Alyssa Chen: latency is a concern for certain features — what sort of latency should we expect over PrivateLink compared to hosted?

[00:07:05] Miguel Alvarez: PrivateLink latency is comparable to cross-AZ L4 hop + NLB; usually single-digit ms added. major determinant is whether inference is on dedicated capacity in same region. hosted multi-tenant in other regions will add more latency. for low-latency use cases we recommend dedicated capacity pinned to the same region/AZ.

[00:07:35] Trevor Miles: any IP allowlist we need on our side? also, are there static ips for endpoint egress?

[00:07:45] Sofia Patel: we can provide ranges for our managed VPC if you're peering; with PrivateLink endpoints the ENIs will have private IPs in your account. For egress to third-parties we can publish static egress IP ranges per region for firewall rules.

[00:08:10] Alyssa Chen: sounds good. on the networking diagram, we have transit gateway + shared services VPC — would Redwood talk to the shared services proxy or directly to per-team VPCs?

[00:08:20] Miguel Alvarez: both options supported — attach interface endpoints in the shared services VPC and route via TGW, or we can do per-account endpoints. we typically recommend a shared endpoint pattern to centralize ops.

[00:08:45] Nina Park: auditability — how granular are logs? do you capture token-level usage? our compliance wants request/response hashes and user identifiers.

[00:08:55] Sofia Patel: we capture request metadata including request id, model, token counts; we can optionally capture request/response hashes for PII tracing. full request/response capture is configurable and subject to retention policies you set.

[00:09:25] Alyssa Chen: ok if we choose dedicated, what's the billing model and can we reserve capacity across regions?

[00:09:35] Sofia Patel: dedicated is reserved monthly/annual commit with predictable throughput; you can buy per-region pools and we support regional failover. pricing and sizing we can put in a follow-up pricing sheet.

[00:09:50] Trevor Miles: more practical: can we run a short benchmark? say a small job to hit 100 concurrent sessions to measure p95 latency and token throughput?

[00:10:00] Miguel Alvarez: absolutely — we do a benchmarking run via a trial VPC peering or PrivateLink in your account. typical steps: provide CIDR ranges and routing, we'll deploy a small test cluster or use dedicated trial nodes and run a scripted load test.

[00:10:20] Alyssa Chen: good. can you also outline the fallback behavior if a model variant is unavailable or if capacity is constrained?

[00:10:30] Sofia Patel: Redwood has smart routing — we can fallback to a smaller model or route to a hosted fallback in a different region based on policy. we'll surface that as part of the rollout config; everything is configurable.

[00:10:50] Nina Park: what's the SSO flow for our users to the Redwood Console if control plane is private? we need SAML integration and SCIM for provisioning.

[00:11:00] Miguel Alvarez: we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. for private control plane we can federate to your IdP; SCIM provisioning is supported for user sync. we'll share the SAML metadata and claim mappings.

[00:11:20] Alyssa Chen: any known gotchas? we've seen issues with DNS and PrivateLink where hostnames resolve to public endpoints during failover.

[00:11:30] Miguel Alvarez: yep DNS is a frequent gotcha. we recommend leveraging Interface endpoint private DNS or explicit Route 53 private hosted zones. during failover to hosted endpoints you may need split-horizon DNS. we'll provide recommended patterns and scripts to switch DNS safely.

[00:12:05] Trevor Miles: about certificate management for TLS on internal endpoints?

[00:12:10] Sofia Patel: certificates can be customer-managed via ACM in your account or we can present certs from our side; for full control use ACM in-account or bring-your-own certs.

[00:12:30] Alyssa Chen: ok that's helpful. any examples of other finance customers with similar setups?

[00:12:35] Sofia Patel: we have a couple: Meridian Capital and Lynx Financial did private VPC deployments with TGW + PrivateLink and KMS integration. we can anonymize diagrams and share references.

[00:12:55] Miguel Alvarez: also worth noting — if you plan to use very long context lengths or heavy KV cache usage, we might recommend specific instance families that have more memory/host RAM; some instance types aren't available in all regions so we'll check availability for eu-west-1.

[00:13:20] Alyssa Chen: good call, we do have a use case for long-context reconciliation jobs.

[00:13:30] Sofia Patel: okay next steps — we'll send the network runbook and an IP cidr template, SOC2/ISO artifacts, and propose a deep-dive time. can we pencil in Jul 8 for a 60-minute technical session?

[00:13:45] Alyssa Chen: Jul 8 works tentatively.

[00:13:50] Trevor Miles: i'll gather the network diagrams and CIDR ranges, and share them before the deep-dive.

[00:14:00] Nina Park: i'll review the SOC docs once you send them and flag any compliance gaps.

[00:14:10] Sofia Patel: perfect. any remaining questions?

[00:14:18] Alyssa Chen: one last — data residency proof — is there a way to get a statement of where logs and data are stored for private deployments?

[00:14:25] Miguel Alvarez: yes we'll include a regional data residency statement in the artifacts pack; for private everything can be pinned to the chosen region and audit logs can be exported to your S3 in-region.

[00:14:45] Sofia Patel: thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and action items.

[00:15:00] (recording auto-notes: transcription has occasional mis-attributions; technical terms may be slightly altered, e.g., "K V cache" for KV cache)

[00:15:15] END OF TRANSCRIPT
